prompt: Please generate an image. Locked painterly style: hand-painted stylized game art, chunky readable shapes, detail painted not modelled, mid-level detail, softer muted colours with gentle saturation, epic and luminous, never grim. The palette's warm gold and cool teal are painted into the surfaces, but the light is flat, even studio light: no strong key light, no cast shadows, no rim light. Use the attached images only as reference as described: the first attachment is always the style reference for palette and brushwork; later attachments are the approved designs to keep. Game-asset reference sheet for 3D modelling, wide landscape 16:9. Plain light neutral grey background, no scene, no sky, no clouds, no floating rock, no ground plane, a soft contact shadow only. Every piece fully isolated with clear space around it, nothing overlapping, nothing touching the edge, arranged in tidy rows, each with a small neat hand-lettered label underneath. MODULAR KIT PIECES sheet: Redraw of the attached reference sheet to the current spec: keep exactly the same pieces, their order, names and sizes. Meadow biome nature kit, 23 pieces, labels exactly as written in quotes, sizes as width x height. Row 1, TREES: "Meadow birch A" 4 x 8 m (single slender white trunk with dark flecks, airy canopy of 4 to 5 yellow-green clumps); "Meadow birch B" 4.5 x 9.5 m (twin trunk forking low, clumps staggered up both stems); "Orchard tree A (apple)" 5 x 4.5 m (short gnarled trunk, round dome canopy with white and pale pink blossom clumps); "Orchard tree B (pear)" 4.5 x 5 m (leaning trunk, denser pink blossom); "Landmark oak A" 18 x 14 m (very thick buttressed trunk with exposed roots on a small mound, broad flat crown wider than tall); "Landmark oak B" 15 x 13 m (rounder compact crown, trunk splits into three limbs, small hollow knot). Row 2, PLANTS AND STONE: "Wildflower drift" 2.5 x 0.9 m (low grass mound with daisies, buttercups, clover and violet lupin spikes); "Flowering bush" 1.6 x 1.4 m (round leafy bush with white and pink wild roses); "Hedgerow, 4 m" 4 x 1.5 m (straight dense yellow-green leaf mass, soft ends); "Standing stone" 1 x 3 m (cream limestone menhir with carved spiral sigil, ivy up one side); "Dry-stone wall, straight 2 m" 2 x 1 m (three to four courses of rough pale cream blocks, moss on top, one 2 m piece only); "Dry-stone wall, corner" 2 x 1 m (L corner with 2 m legs, corner post one block higher). Row 3, GROUND COVER: "Long grass tuft" 0.8 x 0.7 m; "Short grass tuft" 0.6 x 0.2 m; "Clover patch" 0.5 x 0.15 m; "Flower clump" 0.6 x 0.5 m. Row 4, ROCK AND ISLE EDGE: "Limestone rock A" 2.5 x 1.8 m (large rounded cream boulder, lichen on top); "Limestone rock B" 2 x 0.8 m (low stacked flat slabs); "Limestone rock C" 1.6 x 2 m (upright pointed shards around one tall spike); "Limestone rock D" 1.5 x 0.8 m (low mossy dome); "Limestone rock E" 1.6 x 0.6 m (flat cluster of small blocks half sunk in turf); "Limestone lip / ledge" 8 x 3 m (isle edge segment: rounded turf cap over a band of pale limestone blocks, ivy and grass hanging over the face, flat cut ends so segments tile side by side); "Limestone underside taper" 8 x 10 m (inverted wedge of pale layered limestone tapering to a point, turf rim on top, ivy curtains and hanging roots). Pale cream limestone and muted yellow-green foliage throughout, as in the attached sheet. Show each piece as an orthographic front elevation (no perspective) with a small three-quarter view beside it, on faint module grid lines, with its name and size (for example "3 x 4 m") in the label. Thick, solid forms, no thin parts. A plain neutral 1.8 m human silhouette labelled "1.8 m" stands on the sheet for scale, with everything at true scale to it. Title at the top: "Meadow nature kit".
